record_body:
Account summary
- HelixBank (EU HQ). Regulated enterprise bank exploring Redwood Private (VPC) + Dedicated capacity for production workloads.
- Primary theme across stakeholders: strong change management for optimization toggles (batching/caching/quantization/routing) with auditability + rapid rollback.

Contacts / stakeholders (from calls)
- Security/GRC lead: focused on evidentiary audit logs + retention + redaction.
- Platform engineering: wants predictable rollback behavior under partial propagation; doesn’t want “split brain” configs across clusters.
- ML engineering: wants safe rollout patterns (canary + metric gates) for optimization changes; worried about quality regressions.

What they’re building (use case)
- Internal assistant for policy/procedure lookup + summarization of customer case notes.
- Doc-search over internal KB (embeddings + rerank).
- Some chat flows used by call center supervisors (latency sensitivity).

Requirements (key notes)
- Must have immutable config history for optimization config changes (who/what/when/where/why) and ability to rollback in minutes.
- RBAC: separate permissions for apply vs rollback; least-privilege. Preference: on-call SRE role can rollback without being able to edit configs.
- Audit logging: requested event taxonomy includes attempted/applied/failed for apply and rollback; include scope (customer/region/cluster/route/model), request IDs/correlation IDs, and actor (human vs automation).
- Change justification: “We need a reason field and a ticket link, otherwise it won’t pass internal audit.” They asked if Redwood can require justification on rollback.
- Retention: asked for 7-year audit log retention for config change events OR export to their SIEM with their retention. (They have internal requirements similar to SOX-style audit trails; exact policy varies by system.)
- Export: prefers SIEM integration (Splunk) or standard webhook to their logging pipeline; asked about redaction of prompt/customer data (we reiterated audit logs are about config changes, not payloads).
- Progressive delivery: wants canary apply and metric gates (p95 latency, error rate) before full rollout; asked if quality/evals can be attached later.
- Data residency: EU-only processing; Private deployment in their VPC expected.
- KMS: customer-managed keys; standard.

Performance targets (rough)
- P95 latency target for chat endpoints: < 1.2s (excluding downstream app logic), with bursty traffic during business hours.
- Error rate budget: < 0.1% for inference API errors (excluding client errors).
- Throughput expectation: initial ~50–120 RPS mixed workloads; scale planned.

Recent activity timeline
- 2026-01-09: Discovery call (SE + platform eng). Initial interest in Private + Dedicated; emphasized change control.
- 2026-01-23: Shared preliminary security FAQ (stub link) + discussed SSO/SAML and audit log coverage.
- 2026-02-07: Technical deep dive on rollback and auditability. Fireflies: meeting-8f3c1a2b-rollback-and-auditability-deep-dive.
  - Quote from platform lead: “If an optimization tweak blows up latency, we need to roll back in minutes without redeploying the world.”
  - Asked directly about one-click rollback to a known-good version and how we prevent partial propagation.
- 2026-02-13: Follow-up email thread with detailed audit log questions + retention expectations. Gmail: thread-19c2baf4-enterprise-requirements-rollback-audit-logs.
- 2026-02-19: Internal recap with Console team: align on required audit fields, RBAC permissions, and whether justification is mandatory.

Open questions (for Redwood)
- Confirm default retention for config versions and audit events in Private deployments (and what’s configurable).
- Provide written description of rollback semantics: whole-config rollback (no partial rollback in v1), atomic rollout per scope, and behavior under partial failure.
- Clarify “known good” concept: do we allow tagging versions, and can rollback be restricted to versions that passed preflight/metric gates?

Next steps
- SE to share draft audit event schema (apply_attempted/applied/failed, rollback_attempted/rolled_back/failed) and example payload fields.
- Set up joint session with Security Ops (Fiona McCarthy) + Console/Product (Marissa Cole) to walk through: immutable history, RBAC role mapping, and export options.
- If satisfied, move to procurement checklist + plan a VPC Private deployment pilot with limited routes (one chat + embeddings).

Internal notes / risk
- Deal is blocked on audit/change-management assurances more than model quality.
- They will compare to Azure/AWS primarily on compliance posture and operational guardrails.
- Strong signal that Safe apply + rollback mechanism is a must-have for them to move beyond pilot.
